text:
Alicia M: Quick heads-up — healthscore baseline dropped ~18% after last night's CRM import. Noticed it on the onboarding cohort.
Marco V: ugh, thanks. any errors in the import logs?
Priya K: I saw some duplicates in accounts table, might've skewed signal. sample query:
```
SELECT count(*) FROM accounts WHERE created_at >= '2026-03-19' AND crm_import_tag = 'march-migration';
```
Samir R: I can run a dedupe + re-eval backfill. ETA ~1h. @CS Bot can you queue a backfill job that re-calculates healthscore for cohorts created between 03/19-03/21?
CS Bot: job queued by Samir R — job id: job-9923. Estimated runtime 45m. :hourglass:
Marco V: also thinking we should tweak the playbook trigger — current rule fires on healthscore <= 40 but with the import noise we should add a 24h stable window.
Ellen S: Agreed. Proposal:
```
playbook.trigger:
  metric: healthscore
  threshold: 40
  stable_for: 24h
  ignore_tags: ["crm-import"]
```
Priya K: Nice. Also add a dedupe flag into import flow so these temporary bad rows get flagged and excluded from rolling healthscore until backfill completes.
Alicia M: Adding to runbook doc: https://docs.redwood.internal/cs/runbooks/healthscore-imports — please add steps and owner.
Samir R: Backfill job completed successfully. job-9923: 00:38:12 runtime, 12k profiles re-evaluated. :white_check_mark:
CS Bot: alert: rerun of healthscore metrics shows baseline back to expected range (±3%).
Marco V: Awesome. I'll PR the playbook change and add the stable window test to the eval suite.
Priya K: I'll update the import pipeline to set dedupe_flag and emit `crm_import_version` for traceability.
Ellen S: post-mortem note: add a monitoring alert for sudden cohort-wide shifts >10% in 6h.
Alicia M: thanks team — great quick turnaround. :tada:
